newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish fin min Quinn says no need for rate rise.
newsitem.headline: Irish fin min Quinn says no need for rate rise.

text.p: Irish finance minister Ruairi Quinn said on Wednesday there was no immediate inflationary danger and he saw no need for an interest rate rise.
He told Irish radio that inflation data due in two weeks would be benign and there was no need for a rate rise.
"Fears of inflation...would not in my view materialise," Quinn said. "Therefore I do not believe there is any need whatsoever for an interest rate increase."

Asked about the Irish pound's recent fall against sterling, which saw the punt/sterling rate drop to a six-year low on Tuesday, Quinn said the situation was caused by sterling strength rather than punt weakness.

"The pound sterling has risen in value relative to other currencies along with the dollar," he said. "It is not a situation of the Irish pound...falling. The continental currencies and the Irish pound are continuing to converge."
Quinn said he believed economic and monetary union (EMU) would go ahead on time in spite of the victory of the Socialist Party in France's elections.

Irish interest rates were last raised on May 1, when the central bank increased the key short term facility (STF) rate by 50 basis points to 6.75 percent in the aftermath of strong credit growth figures and a sharp drop in the value of the Irish pound.
